s: Fluency first
Squares to 30, cubes to 15, tables to 20, fraction–percent pairs to 1/20. This removes most calculation time.
Think in multipliers
Profit 15% means ×1.15; successive changes multiply. One line, no fractions.
Convert to units
Ratio, mixture, ages, partnership and work: turn quantities into units, solve once, scale back.
Work = LCM units
Set total work to the LCM of the days, so every person’s daily output is a whole number.
Check, don’t redo
Verify with digit sum, unit digit or by putting an option back in. Five seconds, not a re-solve.
Geometry: name the theorem
Draw the figure, mark the givens, name the theorem before touching numbers.
Trigonometry as triangles
Know 30-60-90 (1 : √3 : 2) and 45-45-90 (1 : 1 : √2); most height-and-distance sums become ratios.
DI by estimation
Read title, units and scale first. Round numbers and compare fractions by cross-multiplication.

s: Rule before answer
State the rule in one sentence and test it on every term. If two options fit, the rule is weak.
Letters as numbers
Write A = 1 to Z = 26. Opposite letters sum to 27. Anchors E-J-O-T-Y are 5-10-15-20-25.
Series checklist
Differences, second differences, × or ÷, alternating tracks, squares, cubes, primes, digit sums.
Operations: rewrite first
Swap the symbols exactly as told, rewrite the expression, then apply BODMAS.
Syllogism: always draw
‘Some’ and ‘no’ reverse, ‘all’ does not. Accept only definite conclusions.
Blood relations: tree
One symbol per person, gender only when stated, start from the known person.
Non-verbal: one feature at a time
Count parts, then rotation, shading, position. Mirror flips left–right; water image flips top–bottom.
Folding: undo in reverse
Unfold in the opposite order; holes mirror across each fold line.
f: Sketch the path; net displacement by Pythagoras
Month days ÷ 7; the remainder is the weekday shift

s: Recall questions first
Spelling, one-word substitution, idioms, synonyms and antonyms take seconds. Clear them before grammar and passages.
Vocabulary cards
Word, meaning, two synonyms, one antonym, one phrase. Revise on Day 1, 3, 7, 14, 30.
Read an editorial daily
One editorial plus five new words from it builds vocabulary and passage speed together.
Error spotting: subject and verb
Find them first, then check agreement, tense, article, preposition, pronoun and modifier.
Learn the repeat rules
Each/every/neither + singular; one of + plural noun + singular verb; senior, junior, superior + to; no sooner…than; hardly…when.
Cloze: passage first
Read it once, decide the word type for each blank, test collocation, re-read the full sentence.
RC: find the evidence line
Support every answer with a sentence. Eliminate extremes like always, never, only.
Para-jumbles: pair first
Find the opener (no pronoun, introduces the topic) and fixed pairs, then confirm the flow.
f: Information, furniture, advice, news: singular, no a/an

s: Static first
History, art & culture, science, polity and geography were about 62% of tagged questions. Master them before news.
Facts need hooks
Attach each fact to a map, a timeline or a comparison table. Isolated facts fade.
Recall beats rereading
Closed-book quiz on Day 1, 7 and 30. Wrong at Day 7? Back into the queue.
NCERT for science
School-level biology, physics and chemistry cover most questions: principle plus everyday use.
Polity in context
Learn Part, Article and Schedule together instead of memorising numbers alone.
History as chains
Year, event, leader, place, result. Use timelines for Viceroys, Acts and movements.
Culture by pairs
Dance–state, instrument–artist, temple style–region, heritage site–state.
Current affairs, filtered
Capture schemes, awards, sports, appointments and reports. Verify dates and winners with PIB, RBI, ISRO or the official body.

universalHabits: Tier-I (+2 / −0.5): a guess pays only above 20% chance. Tier-II (+3 / −1): above 25%. Blind 4-option guessing is a small gain in Tier-I and zero in Tier-II, so eliminate one option first.
Tier-I: four wrong answers cancel one correct. Tier-II: three wrong cancel one correct.
In recent cycles Tier-I has acted as a qualifier and merit has come from Tier-II. Verify this in the notification for your cycle, then plan your peak accordingly.
Spend about as long reviewing a mock as taking it. Tag each miss and re-solve after 1 day, 1 week and 3 weeks.
Each section has its own timer, so leftover time cannot move to another section. Use spare minutes to verify, not rush.
Fixed daily study slot, 7+ hours of sleep, and in the last 8 weeks take mocks at your exam-slot hour.
No plan guarantees a rank. A top-10 result needs very high accuracy in every section, a strong Tier-II and a calm exam day. Build the habits you control.
